description: Age-appropriate financial dashboards for Jordan and Casey, scoped to their individual Capital One Money accounts. Simple balance, spending breakdown, and a monthly LLM-generated 'Money Report Card.' Also adds parental side-by-side view of both kids' accounts.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 4 complete (budget framework + category cards). Can be developed in parallel with Feature 5.

principles: Kids see ONLY their own account — no household financial data visible
Keep it simple — teenagers need clarity, not complexity
Money Report Card should feel encouraging, not judgmental
Parent view provides oversight without separate login/permission system

SECRETS INVARIANT — Money Report Card LLM prompts contain only the kid's first name, transaction amounts, merchant names, and categories. Never access tokens, account numbers, .env values, or household financial data. Enforced by secrets-guard.

techStack.testing: Jest for data scoping tests, Playwright for UI isolation verification
techStack.llmProvider: OpenAI API (gpt-5-nano) for Money Report Card

userStories.title: Kids dashboard route and data scoping
acceptanceCriteria: Routes: /pulse/kids/jordan and /pulse/kids/casey
Each route shows ONLY the data for that kid's Capital One Money account
No navigation links to household dashboard, budget, or other accounts
Account linked to kid via configuration (admin assigns account_id to kid profile)
API endpoints for kids data enforce account scoping at query level
userStories.testStrategy: API scoping test: /kids/jordan endpoint returns ONLY Jordan's transactions (zero from other accounts). Negative test: household data not accessible from kids routes.

userStories.title: Kids balance and transaction view
acceptanceCriteria: Current account balance displayed prominently
Recent transactions list (last 30 days, most recent first)
Each transaction: date, merchant, amount
Monthly spending total for current month
Simple, clean design appropriate for teenage users
userStories.testStrategy: UI test: page loads with correct balance and transactions. Monthly total calculation test.

userStories.title: Kids category breakdown
acceptanceCriteria: Simple pie or bar chart: spending by category for current month
Categories simplified for kids: Food & Drinks, Entertainment, Shopping, Personal Care, Other
Chart.js visualization (CDN)
Category totals displayed alongside chart
userStories.testStrategy: Category aggregation test with known transaction data. Chart renders without errors.

userStories.title: Kids monthly budget vs. actual
acceptanceCriteria: Parent-set monthly budget for each kid (admin configuration)
Budget progress bar: spent / total budget
Color coding: green (<70%), yellow (70-99%), red (100%+)
Remaining amount displayed: '$X left this month'
Budget resets monthly
userStories.testStrategy: Budget calculation test. Color threshold test. Monthly reset test.

userStories.title: Money Report Card (LLM narrative)
acceptanceCriteria: Monthly LLM-generated narrative for each kid
Tone: encouraging, educational, age-appropriate (14-16 year olds)
Content: total spent, top categories, biggest purchase, comparison to budget
Example: 'You spent $47 this month. $22 went to food and drinks, $18 to entertainment. Your biggest single purchase was $12 at GameStop.'
Generated on 1st of month, cached in magic_actions_log
Displayed on kids dashboard as a 'card' or collapsible section
No household financial data included in prompt
userStories.testStrategy: Prompt construction test (verify kid-only data, no household info). Mock LLM response rendering test. Tone validation (manual review).

userStories.title: Parental kids overview
acceptanceCriteria: Section on parent dashboard showing both kids' accounts side-by-side
Per kid: balance, monthly spend, budget status, recent transactions (top 5)
Link to full kids dashboard for each child
Only visible on household dashboard (not on kids routes)
userStories.testStrategy: UI test: parental view shows both kids. Data accuracy test: balances match individual kid views.

high: Data scoping failure = kids see household financial data — must have test coverage on data isolation
medium: Kids may not engage if the UI feels like a 'parent monitoring tool' — design for empowerment, not surveillance
LLM tone for teenagers requires careful prompt engineering — too formal = ignored, too casual = not useful
low: Capital One Money accounts may have limited transaction categorization from Plaid

preFlightChecklist: Confirm Jordan and Casey's Capital One Money account IDs in Plaid
Decide: kids budget amounts (Eric to set initial values)
Decide: simplified category list for kids or reuse household categories?
Review: should kids routes have any access control, or Tailscale trust = sufficient?
